preconditions: Code is available and behavior must be preserved.
steps: Inventory entrypoints, tests, and package layout.
Identify domain-like modules, adapters, configuration, and side-effect boundaries.
Trace one representative request/use case from edge to persistence.
Record observed facts separately from proposals.
failure_signs: Recommendations mention files not inspected.
Patterns are proposed before tracing behavior.
stop_conditions: Stop when you can explain one critical workflow and its side effects.
rollback_guidance: Revert exploratory edits; keep only notes/tests.

preconditions: Existing behavior is unclear but must not break.
steps: Find tests, logs, docs, and entrypoints.
Run or read tests if execution is not available.
Create characterization examples around observable input/output.
Label surprising behavior as observed, not desired.
evidence_required: Observed inputs/outputs, state changes, and failures.
failure_signs: Assumptions replace evidence.
Characterization tests assert implementation internals only.
stop_conditions: Stop when current behavior is captured enough for planned change.
rollback_guidance: Remove characterization tests only after desired behavior replaces them deliberately.

preconditions: Bug report has symptom, stack trace, or user scenario.
steps: Minimize inputs and environment required.
Identify where invalid state first appears.
Reproduce with the narrowest test level that exercises the failure.
Record whether failure is expected absence, domain rejection, infrastructure failure, or defect.
evidence_required: Failing command, test, or script; stack trace; input data.
failure_signs: Patch is proposed before reproduction.
Failure only reproduces through broad brittle setup when a smaller seam exists.
stop_conditions: Stop when one deterministic failing test or exact manual reproduction exists.
rollback_guidance: Back out speculative fixes and keep reproduction case.

preconditions: A bug or missing behavior is understood enough to express.
steps: Choose unit/domain/service/integration/E2E level based on failure boundary.
Write the test to fail for the observed reason.
Assert behavior, not incidental implementation.
Then patch the smallest code path.
evidence_required: Test fails before fix and passes after fix.
failure_signs: Test passes before fix.
Test relies on sleeps, network, or unrelated data.
stop_conditions: Stop when failure is locked by a focused test.
rollback_guidance: If test level is too broad, keep it temporarily and add narrower test after seam extraction.

preconditions: Refactor will preserve behavior, not change it.
steps: Select high-value current behaviors.
Capture observable outputs and side effects.
Mark known bugs explicitly if tests preserve them temporarily.
Avoid asserting private implementation.
evidence_required: Representative inputs, outputs, persistence effects, errors.
failure_signs: Tests only mirror code structure.
No rollback plan if behavior changes.
stop_conditions: Stop when refactor risk is covered enough for first slice.
rollback_guidance: Delete or update characterization tests when behavior is intentionally changed.

preconditions: A function mixes decisions with I/O, time, randomness, or persistence.
steps: Identify pure decision inputs and outputs.
Extract pure calculation or domain method.
Inject or pass mechanisms around it.
Unit test pure logic and keep seam/integration test.
evidence_required: Before/after tests; dependency list; extracted function signature.
failure_signs: Extraction changes behavior.
Pure function still reads globals or performs I/O.
stop_conditions: Stop when core decision can run in memory.
rollback_guidance: Inline extraction if it creates no clarity or tests.

preconditions: Tests or changes are blocked by a concrete dependency.
steps: Name the pain: speed, volatility, side effect, or domain leakage.
Define the smallest port/protocol needed by the caller.
Write fake and contract/integration tests.
Move concrete implementation to adapter.
evidence_required: Call sites, fake, real adapter, contract expectations.
failure_signs: Interface mirrors entire vendor/library.
Boundary introduced without a test or change need.
stop_conditions: Stop after one use case uses the new seam safely.
rollback_guidance: Remove port if it becomes unused pass-through.

preconditions: Repeated code differs only by stable parameters or policy.
steps: Check whether duplication hides domain differences.
Extract data/config only for true variation.
Validate configuration at startup or boundary.
Keep policy code typed and tested.
evidence_required: Examples of duplicated branches and intended variation.
failure_signs: Config grows into an untyped rule engine.
Secrets or environment reads scatter.
stop_conditions: Stop when duplication is removed without hiding behavior.
rollback_guidance: Restore explicit branches if config obscures domain rules.

preconditions: A script is reused, tested, or growing side effects.
steps: Separate argument parsing from core function.
Move reusable logic into module with typed boundary.
Inject filesystem/network/config dependencies.
Add tests around core behavior and one CLI/integration path.
failure_signs: Script imports execute work at import time.
Migration creates package ceremony without reuse/tests.
stop_conditions: Stop when core logic is importable without side effects.
rollback_guidance: Keep script wrapper thin and reversible.

preconditions: Existing code is partially or untyped.
steps: Prioritize new, high-churn, high-value, complex, and leaf modules.
Annotate public boundaries first where useful.
Run checker with a staged config.
Track Any and ignores.
evidence_required: Type checker config/report; annotated files; ignored errors list.
failure_signs: Strict mode blocks progress with no plan.
Annotations are broad Any or ceremonial.
stop_conditions: Stop each slice when checker passes and tests still protect behavior.
rollback_guidance: Revert or narrow annotations that misrepresent runtime behavior.

steps: List observed failures: absence, invalid input, domain rejection, infrastructure, programming defect.
Choose Optional/result/exception per caller recovery needs.
Update public signatures/docs/tests.
Translate errors at adapters.
evidence_required: Failure examples and caller handling expectations.
failure_signs: All failures become None or RuntimeError.
Infrastructure errors leak to external callers.
stop_conditions: Stop when tests cover each public failure mode.
rollback_guidance: Roll back broad hierarchy if it adds no caller value.

preconditions: Persistence details make domain/application tests slow or coupled.
steps: Choose one aggregate/use case.
Define smallest repository port.
Add fake for service tests and real adapter integration/contract test.
Do not move commit policy into repository.
evidence_required: Existing persistence coupling; fake/real tests; service using port.
failure_signs: Repository duplicates ORM without reducing pain.
One repository per table appears by default.
stop_conditions: Stop after one workflow uses repository and tests are clearer.
rollback_guidance: Inline repository if it remains unused pass-through.

preconditions: Entrypoint mixes protocol, persistence, and domain decisions.
steps: Pick one endpoint/use case.
Create typed command/input object if helpful.
Move orchestration to service; keep domain rules in model/functions.
Test service with fake dependencies and keep entrypoint test thin.
evidence_required: Before/after entrypoint; service tests; error mapping.
failure_signs: Service only forwards calls.
Domain rules migrate into orchestration without reason.
stop_conditions: Stop when one entrypoint is thinner and behavior preserved.
rollback_guidance: Move logic back if service adds no responsibility.

steps: State intended behavior change: none or specific.
Add tests before moving code.
Make one small change at a time.
Run relevant checks after each slice.
Record rollback.
evidence_required: Passing tests before/after; diff scoped to one responsibility.
failure_signs: Big-bang rename and behavior edits in one patch.
No rollback path.
stop_conditions: Stop when the demonstrated problem is solved; do not continue pattern migration for aesthetics.
rollback_guidance: Revert last slice; keep tests if valid.

preconditions: Code is ugly but stable or refactor value is unclear.
steps: Identify concrete pain: bugs, test cost, change cost, performance, security, or comprehension risk.
Estimate smallest safe improvement.
If no evidence exists, document non-action and monitor.
evidence_required: Bug frequency, change history, test pain, team feedback.
failure_signs: Refactor justified only by taste or pattern preference.
Leaving known high-risk code untouched without mitigation.
rollback_guidance: Create a revisit condition rather than speculative patch.
